claim.pdf_says: 9.1.13.8   Record operation conflict condition with unsuccessful completion  (a fourth-level subclause of 9.1.13, peer of 9.1.13.7 and 9.1.13.9)
claim.markdown_says: ## 9.1.13.8 Record operation conflict condition with unsuccessful completion  (whereas its immediate neighbours read '### 9.1.13.7 Logic error condition with unsuccessful completion' and '### 9.1.13.9 File sharing conflict condition with unsuccessful completion')
claim.why_it_matters: Same outline break as 9.1.13.2: the heading is one level shallower than its siblings, so 9.1.13.9, 9.1.13.10 and 9.1.13.11 become children of 9.1.13.8 in any generated TOC. No normative content is affected.

verdict.reasoning: Tried to refute on every available ground and could not. (1) The heading is NOT missing text and is NOT reflowed or split across a page break: the PDF page 258 (printed folio 228) prints it intact on one line, '9.1.13.8   Record operation conflict condition with unsuccessful completion', immediately after item 9) of 9.1.13.7 and immediately before item 1) 'I-O status = 51.' The markdown carries the identical wording on line 11457 of specs/ISO_COBOL.md (line 37 of the page-258 slice). So this is purely a heading-LEVEL defect, not lost text. (2) The claim does not misquote either source. I rendered the two neighbouring pages to check the sibling headings at their own printed locations: page 257 (folio 227) prints '9.1.13.7   Logic error condition with unsuccessful completion', and page 259 (folio 229) prints '9.1.13.9   File sharing conflict condition with unsuccessful completion', '9.1.13.10   Record with invalid content with unsuccessful completion' and '9.1.13.11   Implementor-defined condition with unsuccessful completion'. All five headings are set in visually IDENTICAL typography: same bold serif face, same point size, same left margin flush with the body-text left edge, same wide gap between number and title. There is no typographic distinction whatsoever that would justify the markdown promoting 9.1.13.8 above its siblings. (3) The difference is not formatting furniture and it does change structure: the ISO clause number '9.1.13.8' is unambiguously four levels deep, exactly as deep as 9.1.13.7 and 9.1.13.9, so a '##' on it is objectively wrong regardless of how the PDF is styled. (4) The grep over specs/ISO_COBOL.md confirms the anomaly is isolated and exactly as described - 9.1.13.1 '###', 9.1.13.2 '##' (the sibling defect the claim references), 9.1.13.3 through 9.1.13.7 all '###', 9.1.13.8 '##', 9.1.13.9 through 9.1.13.11 all '###'. Only .2 and .8 are mis-leveled. (5) The stated consequence is accurate: since the parent 9.1.13 is itself '##', a '##' 9.1.13.8 is emitted as a SIBLING of its own parent, and the '###' headings that follow it (9.1.13.9, .10, .11) nest underneath it in any generated TOC. (6) Severity 'cosmetic' is right - I compared the full body of page 258 against the transcription (items 3 through 9 of 9.1.13.7 including all sub-items a-d of item 4, a-b of item 6, a-b of item 8, plus item 1 of 9.1.13.8) and the normative text is complete and faithful; only the curly quotes around '06' are flattened, which is formatting.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, with two refinements to the description. First, the defect is a heading-LEVEL error only, not missing text: the heading's wording is present and verbatim-correct in the markdown ('## 9.1.13.8 Record operation conflict condition with unsuccessful completion', specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 11457), so the kind is better characterized as 'heading-level' than 'missing-heading'. Second, the structural damage is slightly worse than stated: because the parent clause 9.1.13 is itself transcribed as '## 9.1.13 I-O status', giving 9.1.13.8 a '##' does not merely make it shallower than its siblings - it detaches it from its own parent and emits it as a SIBLING of 9.1.13, on par with 9.1.12 and 9.1.14. The three following subclauses 9.1.13.9, 9.1.13.10 and 9.1.13.11 (all correctly '###') then nest under 9.1.13.8 instead of under 9.1.13, exactly as claimed. Independently verified against the printed page: PDF page 258 (folio 228) sets '9.1.13.8   Record operation conflict condition with unsuccessful completion' in the same bold serif, same point size and same left margin as '9.1.13.7   Logic error condition with unsuccessful completion' on page 257 (folio 227) and '9.1.13.9   File sharing conflict condition with unsuccessful completion' on page 259 (folio 229) - there is no typographic basis in the source for the promotion. The fix is a one-character change of '##' to '###' on line 11457; the identical fix is needed on line 11290 for 9.1.13.2, which is the only other member of the 9.1.13.1-9.1.13.11 run with the same defect. No normative content is affected.
